transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Thank you. Um… I’m here because I’ve been having trouble putting worries aside. It’s probably not as dramatic as that sounds, but once something gets in my head—like my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work—I just can’t seem to shelve it, if that makes sense. I make lists and try to redirect myself, but it keeps circling back.
Do you notice any physical symptoms when these worries come up, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but I do notice my body gets kind of tight. By the end of the day my neck and shoulders feel almost locked up, like I’ve been bracing myself without realizing it. And I catch myself clenching my jaw sometimes, especially when I’m answering emails or sort of listening for my mother in the next room. Does that make sense?
Do you find that your worrying happens more often than not, like most days, and does it feel hard to control even when you try?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m worried every single second, but most days, once something gets started in my head—my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work—I have a really hard time setting it aside. I’ll make lists, or tell myself I’ve handled what I can, but it still keeps coming back. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends or family?

Um… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a big change like that, at least not clearly. I still care about the things I usually care about, and I don’t think I’m, you know, unable to enjoy people or hobbies. Maybe I’m a little preoccupied sometimes, but I’m not sure that’s the same as feeling down. Is that what you mean?
Have you found yourself doing certain things over and over, like checking, counting, or repeating actions, because it helps quiet the thoughts or makes you feel more in control?

I don’t think so… not in that sense. I mean, I do check my calendar or make lists sometimes, but it doesn’t feel like I’m counting things or repeating actions until something feels “right,” if that’s what you mean. It’s more just trying to stay organized, I think. I haven’t really noticed anything like that.

Have you noticed any thoughts that keep coming into your mind, even when you don’t want them to—like fears of making a mistake, harming someone accidentally, or something bad happening—even if you know they might not make much sense?

I don’t think so… not like thoughts that feel strange or scary in that way. I do worry about mistakes or something going wrong, but it usually feels connected to real things I’m responsible for, if that makes sense. I’m not having thoughts about harming anyone or anything like that. It’s more… everyday worries getting stuck, maybe. Is that different from what you’re asking?
Can you describe how long these worries typically last once they start? Do they tend to linger for hours, or is it more like background tension that's just there most of the time?

It’s… more than I’d like to admit, I guess. Once something gets in my head—like worrying about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work—I can’t really just put it away. I make lists, and I try to redirect myself, and I tell myself it’s probably fine, but it keeps sort of running in the background… sometimes for hours. Maybe longer, depending on the day. Does that make sense?
Do these worries ever get in the way of your daily life—like making it harder to focus at work, be present with family, or enjoy your time—even if you’re trying your best to manage them?

Yes… I think it has, a bit. I mean, I’m still functioning—I don’t want to make it sound dramatic—but I’ve started missing small details at the library, the kind of things I really don’t usually miss. And there was a grant presentation where I just… froze, and I had to hand off parts of it to someone else.

That’s been hard to admit, honestly, because I’m usually the person people can count on. So now I’m worrying about whether I’m still leading my team well. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
